title: Key Concepts: Pods, Deployments, Services 🧩
description: Get a bird’s‑eye view of the three most important Kubernetes objects.

slides.title: The Building Blocks 🧱
slides.content:
# Three concepts you’ll use daily

- **Pod** – smallest deployable unit; a wrapper around one or more containers
- **Deployment** – manages a set of identical Pods, handles updates
- **Service** – stable network endpoint to access a set of Pods

Understanding these will unlock 80% of Kubernetes.

slides.title: Pod – the Atomic Unit ⚛️
slides.content:
## What’s inside a Pod?

A Pod can contain one or more containers that:
- Share the same network namespace (localhost works between them)
- Share storage volumes
- Are always co‑located on the same node

Most often, a Pod runs a single main container. Sidecar containers (like log shippers) are also common.

quizData.question: What is the smallest deployable unit in Kubernetes?
quizData.explanation: A Pod is the atom of Kubernetes—you cannot deploy a container without a Pod.

slides.title: Deployment – the Scalable Manager 🎛️
slides.content:
## Why you need more than a Pod

Pods are ephemeral. If a node dies, Pods on it are lost. A **Deployment** ensures:
- A specified number of replica Pods are always running
- Rolling updates with zero downtime
- Ability to rollback to a previous version

It creates a ReplicaSet, which in turn creates/ deletes Pods.

quizData.question: What does a Deployment guarantee?

options.text: That Pods are scheduled on the fastest node
A desired number of replica Pods are always running
That every Pod gets a persistent IP

quizData.explanation: Deployments maintain the replica count and handle updates.

slides.title: Service – Stable Networking 🔌
slides.content:
## Pods come and go, IPs change

A **Service** provides:
- A stable IP address (ClusterIP)
- A DNS name
- Load balancing across the Pods selected by labels

Types: ClusterIP (internal), NodePort (node‑level access), LoadBalancer (cloud provider).

slides.title: Connecting Them
slides.content: Example: A Deployment manages Pods, a Service selects them by label:
slides.codeSnippet:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nginx-service
spec:
  selector:
    app: nginx
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 80

quizData.question: How does a Service know which Pods to send traffic to?
quizData.explanation: Services use label selectors to find the right Pods.
